dream: The card hummed at fifty-three while I pressed the lid down, hoping the heavy top felt real. I sat on a grass that felt like a drawing of a cushion, soft and heavy at once. The wedge slid sideways, biting into the sand, while the flat rock leaned wrong against the fence. I traced the rim of the lid with my thumb, wondering if the air was thick as wet paper. Then the wedge slipped again, and the grass stretched into a long, thin strip, pulling the whole world into a single, flat line.
